newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins ease in nervous trade.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins ease in nervous trade.

text.p: Russian markets pushed prices of MinFin bonds down slightly on Wednesday, nervous about President Boris Yeltsin's expected heart surgery and hungry for fresh news of Russia's forthcoming Eurobond issue, dealers said.

"The market is weaker today because of nervousness on lack of news about the Eurobond issue following Russia's rating," a Western bank dealer said and added the market was also focusing on Yeltsin's health.
Russia received a high but subinvestment grade rating last week and Russia's first Eurobond issue is expected this year.
"The market is quite volatile. Selling is nervous but in small amounts," the dealer said.
The head of the Kremlin medical centre said on Wednesday doctors will operate on Yeltsin's heart in mid-November, as planned. Earlier estimates had put the surgery as much as one month later.

"Some Russian banks were earlier buying actively, especially the fifth tranche but it failed to go higher than 42.00... Prices are fluctuating now both ways, gently edging down," Avtobank dealer Ivan Kuznetsov said.
He added the most liquid fourth and fifth tranches were not easing lower than 58.10 and 41.10 respectively.
